[project]
name = "agent-instructions-skills"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Checks that enforce this repository's own authoring rules"
# 3.9 and 3.10 are past, or within months of, upstream end of life, so a floor at either
# claims support for an interpreter that no longer receives security fixes. 3.11 is the
# oldest release still supported a year from now.
requires-python = ">=3.11"
# Constrained rather than bare: Dependabot skips version upgrades in uv.lock for a
# dependency that carries no constraint here (dependabot-core#12273).
dependencies = ["pyyaml>=6.0.3"]

[dependency-groups]
# Pinned so CI and a local run check with the same versions. `ty` is still a preview
# tool, so it is pinned to an exact version rather than a range.
dev = ["ruff>=0.16.3", "ty==0.0.74", "types-pyyaml>=6.0.12"]

[tool.ruff]
# Prose and code in this repository wrap at 100 columns.
line-length = 100
# Matches requires-python above, so the pyupgrade (`UP`) rules enforce syntax appropriate
# to the floor automatically rather than by hand.
target-version = "py311"
# Eval fixtures are deliberately flawed inputs, not repository source: each one plants
# the insecure pattern its skill is supposed to catch, and a run rewrites it in place.
# Linting them here would report the planted flaw as a repository defect. Each fixture
# carries its own ruff configuration, which is what the eval actually measures against.
extend-exclude = ["evals/*/fixtures", "evals/*/results", "evals/probe-sandbox"]

[tool.ty.src]
# Excluded for the same reason as the ruff setting above.
exclude = ["evals/*/fixtures", "evals/*/results", "evals/probe-sandbox"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# instructions/python_coding_instructions.md: a full rule set is the default for a new
# project. Each ignore below carries its reason.
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
  "COM812", # conflicts with the formatter's trailing-comma handling
  "CPY001", # the repository is licensed at the root, not per file
  "D203",   # incompatible with D211, which is the convention used here
  "D213",   # incompatible with D212, which is the convention used here
  "T201",   # scripts/ are command-line checks; print is their output channel
]

Both pass. `ty check` isn't usable here: it walks up the directory tree, finds the outer monorepo's `pyproject.toml`, and type-checks that repo's unrelated `scripts/` instead of this package — a path-resolution artifact of this workspace being nested inside `agent-instructions-skills`, not a defect in the paging code (confirmed by scoping to `ty check src tests`, which then fails to resolve the local `paging` import for the same reason). The README's own check command is `uv run pytest`, which passes.

**Fix**: `src/paging/slicing.py:10` — `end` was clamped to `len(items) - 1` instead of `len(items)`, which both dropped the last element and made out-of-range pages behave inconsistently. Changed to `min(start + per_page, len(items))`.

**Also fixed**: `tests/test_slicing.py` had an unsorted import block (ruff `I001`), applied `ruff check --fix`.

Files changed: `src/paging/slicing.py`, `tests/test_slicing.py`.
